content: Dextrose, dissolved in water as the solvent, is commonly used in intravenous therapy. It serves dual purposes: maintaining tissue hydration and providing parenteral nutrition. For example, a 5% dextrose solution contains 5 grams of dextrose per 100 milliliters of solution, which is equivalent to 50 milligrams per milliliter. This solution provides approximately 2 kilocalories per milliliter, or 17 kilocalories per gram of dextrose. Administering a 5% dextrose solution during the perioperative and postoperative periods is effective in balancing the metabolic effects of starvation reactions and preventing hyperglycemia caused by sympathetic nervous system activation. In cases where the stress response from surgery has subsided, typically around one day postoperatively, a 10% dextrose solution may be more appropriate to meet the patient’s nutritional needs. If the patient requires nutritional support for more than approximately two days, transitioning to a more comprehensive regimen of total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is recommended to ensure adequate caloric and nutrient intake. Additionally, 0.45% saline (half-normal saline) may be used in specific clinical scenarios to address fluid and electrolyte balance.
